question: Can LLM-as-judge rubrics be trusted to grade production agent output?

sides.stance: Yes, once evaluators are meta-evaluated against human-labeled golden datasets until judge and human verdicts align before deployment.
Yes, for post-merge conversation grading across efficiency, code quality, and test coverage rubrics that surface recurring harness bottlenecks.
Only with cross-family judges and two-stage categorical buckets, because model families exhibit strong self-preference bias.
No for standalone verification: LLM verdicts flip 7–17% across identical runs and up to 34% when challenged with 'are you sure?'
No when deterministic checks are achievable: LLM-judge noise rivaled the agent's own error rate, motivating architectural redesign around ground-truth checks.

question: Do spatiotemporal world models learn control from passive video prediction alone, or do they require explicit action labels?

sides.stance: Next-frame video prediction at scale internalizes geometry, gravity, occlusion, and object permanence directly from pixels to power interactive world simulators.
Explicit controller action labels transfer far better to real-time control because subtle high-frequency inputs like rudder adjustments cannot be inferred from video frames alone.

question: Should enterprises own open, model-swappable foundations or scale atop frontier lab platforms?

sides.stance: Own open foundations: commoditizing token margins force frontier labs up into the enterprise agent layer and vertical markets to capture switching-cost stickiness.
Go a layer below frontier APIs now: pairing a frontier orchestrator with a post-trained 35B open specialist beat the frontier on exact-pass accuracy at lower latency.
Scale a shared foundation on frontier models: raw model capability and unit cost are no longer the bottleneck—organizational deployment from one-to-many is.
Weigh the Bitter Lesson carefully: unit token economics keep falling automatically as newer, friendlier frontier models ship.

question: Where does human review belong once coding and workflow agents run autonomously?

sides.stance: At mandatory mutation sign-off: financial agents operate with least-privilege identity and propose amendments that a human SME must approve before execution.
Only on genuinely ambiguous escalations: approving every action induces rubber-stamp fatigue, so deterministic fast paths and classifiers should handle routine calls.
At the behavioral proof gate: builders loop autonomously with reviewer agents, but a human product owner must watch each recorded feature video before merge.
Above line-by-line code reading: high-confidence automated merges rely on end-to-end, property-based, and visual verification rather than manual diff inspection.

question: Will frontier models absorb the agent harness, or must builders keep engineering scaffolding and process around them?

sides.stance: Models absorb coding scaffolding via the data flywheel: trajectories generated through today's harness train tomorrow's weights until harness choice stops moving coding accuracy.
Opinionated process stays outside the weights: open-ended agents produce inconsistent enterprise work unless builders encode explicit domain workflow specs.
Every unmastered frontier re-inflates the harness: autonomous multi-agent knowledge workers immediately require coordinator hierarchies, new prompting, and guardrails.
Outer-loop context remains irreducible: cheap code shifts failure to product incoherence because source code alone never holds customer intent, ownership, or revert history.
